C-BROWSER-TABS-HISTORY-SERVICES-20260901.Summary:
Deliver the first bounded M1.3 browser-service slice: establish the common browser-service plugin architecture and implement independent tabs and durable-history services above the existing M1.2 browser engine provider.
The change introduces only experimental 0.1 service contracts, preserves Browser Contract v1 and the CEF provider boundary unchanged, and proves that user-level tab state and durable history can crash, restart and evolve independently from page navigation and engine state.
C-BROWSER-TABS-HISTORY-SERVICES-20260901.Problem:
M1.2 provides production browser-engine primitives, logical ContextId/PageId, navigation, typed browser events, persistence and recovery, but Worldline still has no product-level tab model or durable user-history service.
Chromium back/forward state is an engine recovery primitive rather than a durable history source of truth. Likewise, a PageId is an engine resource identity rather than a tab identity.
Implementing all M1.3 services in one change would mix unrelated authority, persistence and failure domains. The first service slice must therefore establish the reusable service-plugin boundary with the two lowest-coupling services: tabs and history.

Goals.Goal: Record the common M1.3 browser-service architecture, contract-stability policy, source-of-truth rules and failure-isolation model in docs/adr/ADR-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS-V1.md.
Add an engine-neutral experimental service-contract surface for tabs and history without adding CEF, CDP, HWND or browser-provider implementation types.
Implement an ordinary tabs plugin that owns TabId, ordering, grouping, pinning and user-level selection while referencing existing PageId values.
Implement an ordinary durable history plugin that consumes committed navigation facts and owns persistent user-history records.
Prove tabs and history can restart independently without terminating, recreating or corrupting underlying browser pages.
Establish the BrowserServices CI foundation and one bounded real-provider S3A integration path for later M1.3 service bundles.

Constraints.Constraint: SPEC APPROVAL AND EXACT PLAN APPROVAL REMAIN SEPARATE; THIS DRAFT DOES NOT AUTHORIZE IMPLEMENTATION AND NO PLAN IS APPROVED BY THIS SPEC.
C-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS-20260901 MUST BE EXPLICITLY APPLIED AND ARCHIVED BEFORE THE PLAN FOR THIS CHANGE IS APPROVED OR EXECUTED.
BROWSER SERVICES ARE ORDINARY PLUGINS; NO TAB OR HISTORY PRODUCT POLICY MAY ENTER THE KERNEL OR RECEIVE A BROWSER-SPECIFIC PRIVILEGED PATH.
THIS CHANGE DOES NOT MODIFY CEF BEHAVIOR, NATIVE PROVIDER PROCESS SEMANTICS OR THE STABLE BROWSER CONTRACT V1.0 REQUEST/RESPONSE WIRE FORMS.
NEW BROWSER SERVICE CONTRACTS START AS EXPERIMENTAL VERSION 0.1. THIS CHANGE MUST NOT CLAIM V1 STABILITY.
SERVICE CONTRACT TYPES MAY REUSE ENGINE-NEUTRAL IDs FROM worldline-browser-contract BUT MUST NOT DEPEND ON worldline-browser-cef OR PROVIDER-PRIVATE TYPES.
TabId, TabGroupId AND TAB MEMBERSHIP ARE SERVICE IDENTITIES/STATE; NONE OF THEM CONFER PageId AUTHORITY.
CLOSING OR REMOVING A TAB DOES NOT CLOSE THE UNDERLYING PageId. PAGE CLOSURE REQUIRES A SEPARATE AUTHORIZED browser.page OPERATION.
THE TABS SERVICE MUST NOT REQUIRE NavigatePage, ActOnPage OR QueryDocument AUTHORITY TO STORE OR REORDER TAB REFERENCES.
HISTORY OBSERVES BROWSER FACTS THROUGH EVENT TRANSPORT; IT DOES NOT DISPATCH NAVIGATION AND EVENT BUS IS NOT RPC.
THE EVENT JOURNAL AND CHROMIUM BACK/FORWARD STACK ARE NOT THE AUTHORITATIVE USER-HISTORY DATABASE.

NavigationCommittedEvent REMAINS WIRE-COMPATIBLE. HISTORY MUST NOT CHANGE THAT STABLE EVENT MERELY TO ADD A TITLE; OPTIONAL TITLE ENRICHMENT MAY USE browser.page.ready OR A SEPARATELY AUTHORIZED OBSERVATION.
AT-LEAST-ONCE EVENT REDELIVERY MUST NOT CREATE DUPLICATE LOGICAL HISTORY ENTRIES.
HISTORY CAUSALITY IS BASED ON TRUSTED EVENT/INVOCATION IDENTITIES SUCH AS NavigationId AND EVENT METADATA, NOT TIMESTAMP PROXIMITY.
PROTECTED M0, M1.1 AND M1.2 ACCEPTANCE TESTS MUST NOT BE WEAKENED, SKIPPED OR REWRITTEN TO MAKE THIS CHANGE GREEN.
TEST AND PROVING NETWORK CONTENT IS LOCAL/LOOPBACK; NO PUBLIC INTERNET IS REQUIRED.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Cookies service implementation or cookie-value policy.
Worldline Shell or final tab-bar UI.
Bookmarks, sessions, passwords, autofill or reading list.
Automatically closing a PageId when a TabId is closed.
Promoting any new M1.3 service contract to stable v1.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: docs/adr/ADR-BROWSER-SERVICE-PLUGINS-V1.md documents the service/plugin boundary, experimental-contract policy, independent sources of truth, degraded composition rules, TabId versus PageId semantics, engine navigation versus durable history, and the planned M1.3 bundle sequence.

A new engine-neutral contract crate or equivalent isolated contract surface exposes browser.tabs experimental 0.1 and browser.history experimental 0.1 without dependencies on CEF, CDP or provider-private crates.

Tabs authority distinguishes at minimum read/list authority from mutation authority; possession of a PageId value or TabId mapping does not satisfy browser.page, browser.navigate, browser.query or browser.act authority.
Tabs service defines opaque TabId and TabGroupId identities and persists TabId-to-PageId membership, ordering, grouping, pinned state and selected TabId as its own transactional source of truth.
Tabs operations cover create/attach, list/get, select, move, pin/unpin, group/ungroup and close/detach semantics through versioned capability RPC.
Closing/detaching a TabId removes only tabs-service state; an acceptance test proves the referenced PageId remains alive and usable until a separately authorized browser.page close occurs.
Tabs-service restart restores its persisted projection and reconciles references against currently available PageIds without manufacturing missing pages or browser authority.
External browser.page.closed facts may cause deterministic tab reconciliation, but a tabs event subscriber cannot issue an implicit page-close or navigation command.
History service owns a transactional durable source of truth containing at minimum HistoryEntryId, PageId, NavigationId, DocumentRevision, URL, trusted commit metadata and optional title enrichment.
browser.navigation.committed creates one logical durable history entry keyed by the committed navigation identity; repeated delivery of the same event or NavigationId is idempotent.
A duplicate logical navigation carrying conflicting immutable commit fields is reported as an explicit consistency error rather than silently overwriting the authoritative history entry.
browser.page.ready may enrich the title of the matching PageId + DocumentRevision record without changing the original committed navigation identity or requiring a stable browser-event wire change.
History service exposes separately authorized read/query and destructive delete/clear operations; observing history never grants NavigatePage.
Deleting or clearing history affects only the history service source of truth and does not clear cookies, storage, browser profiles, PageIds or the engine back/forward stack.
History-service restart restores durable records and its delivery checkpoint/deduplication state so a redelivered committed navigation remains one logical history entry.
Killing the history plugin leaves direct browser navigation operational; killing the tabs plugin leaves existing PageIds operational.
Generic operational metrics for tabs/history contain no page body, form input, cookie values or other private browser payloads.
Static architecture checks prove worldline-kernel and worldline-browser-cef do not depend on TabId, HistoryEntryId or the tabs and history plugin implementations.
Unit and integration acceptance suites cover authority separation, persistence, duplicate delivery, restart, page-detach semantics and optional-service failure isolation.
A repository-owned BrowserServices CI suite runs the service-contract, tabs and history acceptance tests cross-platform without public network access.

One bounded Windows S3A path uses the real M1.2 provider through normal capabilities: create a PageId, attach it to a TabId, navigate a loopback page, durably record the committed navigation, restart the history service, verify the record survives, remove the tabs service and verify the PageId still works.

Source, Correctness, ArchitectureSecurity, ProvingSlice, RealChromium, BrowserProvider and All remain green, and fresh hosted evidence names the BrowserServices/S3A run rather than promoting local evidence.

After fresh evidence and explicit apply confirmation, GRACE may add M-BROWSER-TABS-SERVICE and M-BROWSER-HISTORY-SERVICE with corresponding verification entries; M1.3 remains Active rather than being marked Done.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Fresh evidence names experimental 0.1 contract fixtures, tabs authority negative tests, tab-detach/page-survival evidence, history transactional persistence, at-least-once deduplication, restart recovery, optional service failure isolation, the real-provider S3A path and a required hosted BrowserServices run. Local results remain labelled local.

Assumptions.Assumption: C-BROWSER-ENGINE-PROVIDER-PROCESS-20260901 is explicitly confirmed applied and archived before this change's plan is approved or executed.
The accepted M1.2 provider boundary and Browser Contract v1 remain valid; this slice consumes them rather than reopening CEF/provider architecture.
Existing browser.navigation.committed and browser.page.ready facts are sufficient for initial durable history without adding title to the committed-event wire form.
New service contracts remain experimental 0.1 until later M1 consumers provide evidence for compatibility stabilization.

The exact physical persistence schema is selected in the separately approved plan, but tabs and history retain independent transactional sources of truth and may not use the event journal as authoritative state.
Downloads/cookies, request-policy/adblock, diagnostics/search and final S3 closure are separately governed follow-on changes.
